title: Speak: first phrases
description: Sound first. Say useful phrases before you can read them.

units.title: Hello and goodbye
intro: You can start speaking before you can read. This path is sound first.
Each phrase is shown in romaji (English letters) so you can say it. The Japanese writing is shown small underneath. Do not worry about reading it yet.
Japanese is spoken in even beats. Give every syllable the same length, and do not stress one harder than the others.
Tap the speaker and repeat out loud. Saying it matters more than tapping the right answer.

items.hint: The daytime hello. Even beats: kon-ni-chi-wa. Hold the first n a little.
'ou' is one long 'oh', not 'oh-oo': o-ha-yoh. Add 'gozaimasu' after it to be polite.
sa-yoh-na-ra. A real goodbye, for when you will not meet again soon. With friends, people often say 'ja ne'.

units.title: Yes, no, thank you
intro: Five short phrases that carry most simple exchanges.
The Japanese r is a quick tap of the tongue behind the top teeth, close to a soft d. You will hear it in 'arigatou'.

items.hint: Sounds like the English word 'hi'. Short and crisp.
a-ri-ga-toh. The 'ou' at the end is one long 'oh'.
su-mi-ma-sen. Use it to get attention, to apologize, or to squeeze past someone.
o-ne-gai-shi-mas. The last u is almost silent. Say it when you ask for something.

units.title: Getting by
intro: Three phrases for shops, restaurants and moments when you are lost.
A 'ka' at the end of a sentence turns it into a question. Your voice does not need to rise.

items.hint: i-ku-ra des-ka. 'desu' sounds like 'des'. The 'ka' makes it a question.
o-i-shee. The double i is one long 'ee'. Say it when the food is good.
